summary:
SPHEREx Deep Space Explorer is an interactive, browser-based astronomy tool developed by Interstellar Consortium for NASA's Planet X and SPHEREx challenge.
NASA's SPHEREx mission maps the entire sky in 102 near-infrared wavelength bands, completing an all-sky survey approximately every six months. These extensive datasets provide valuable opportunities for astronomical exploration but can be challenging to inspect and compare.
Our web application provides an intuitive, Google Maps-style interface with three core capabilities: an Interactive Sky Sphere for exploring celestial coordinates, an Infrared and Multi-Epoch Comparison View for examining spectral information and changes across observations, and a Searchable Object Table powered directly by official NASA SPHEREx challenge resources.
By combining astronomical imagery, coordinate-based exploration, and structured metadata from official challenge datasets, SPHEREx Deep Space Explorer makes infrared astronomy more accessible to students, citizen scientists, and researchers. The application serves strictly as an exploratory visualization tool, not a claim of confirmed Planet X detection.
details:
Project Details – SPHEREx Deep Space Explorer

The Problem:

NASA's SPHEREx mission surveys the entire sky across 102 near-infrared spectral bands every six months, generating vast astronomical datasets. Exploring these observations, navigating celestial coordinates, and comparing changes across different observation periods can be difficult for students, citizen scientists, and researchers without specialized archive tools.

Our Proposed Solution:

SPHEREx Deep Space Explorer is an interactive, browser-based astronomical exploration tool developed by Interstellar Consortium. It brings official SPHEREx challenge datasets, sky imagery, and object metadata together into an intuitive, Google Maps-style interface.

How It Works:

Powered directly by official NASA/IPAC SPHEREx challenge resources, the application organizes astronomical imagery and structured metadata into three streamlined features:

- Interactive Sky Sphere: Enables users to pan, zoom, and explore celestial coordinates visually.

- Infrared & Multi-Epoch Comparison View: Allows users to inspect near-infrared spectral information and compare observations across different time periods to spot positional shifts.

- Searchable Object Table: Provides instant filtering and inspection of object IDs, celestial coordinates (RA/Dec), and brightness metrics from the official challenge datasets.

Technologies and Resources:

The web interface is built using modern browser-based technologies (HTML, CSS, and JavaScript) alongside official NASA/IPAC IRSA SPHEREx resources and astronomical data-processing workflows (Python, Astropy, Astroquery, and NumPy) used during data preparation.

Innovation and Impact:

By combining visual sky exploration with structured coordinate metadata in a clean, accessible web tool, SPHEREx Deep Space Explorer lowers the technical barrier to infrared astronomy—helping students, astronomy enthusiasts, and researchers explore open NASA sky-survey data.

Scientific Limitations:

SPHEREx Deep Space Explorer is an exploratory visualization and educational tool, not a claim of confirmed Planet X detection. Any moving object or candidate signature observed in survey data requires independent astronomical follow-up and scientific validation.
